MCP servers architecture on solidPC (2026-04 setup):

ARCHITECTURE:

- Configs at /shared/config/mcp-<name>/

- 32769: searxng (uses sacode/searxng-simple-mcp directly, env TRANSPORT_PROTOCOL=streamable-http)
- 32770: MCPJungle gateway (aggregator, currently unused)

DOCKERFILE PATTERN for new mcp-proxy-based server:
FROM ghcr.io/sparfenyuk/mcp-proxy:latest
RUN apk add --no-cache nodejs npm && npm install -g <pkg>  # for Node servers
# OR for Python: ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/app/.venv PATH=/app/.venv/bin:$PATH; RUN python -m ensurepip && python -m pip install --no-cache-dir <pkg>
ENTRYPOINT ["mcp-proxy", "--stateless", "--port", "<port>", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--", "<command>"]

KEY GOTCHAS:
- mcp-proxy base image is Alpine with Python 3.13 — use apk not apt, install node via apk
- Python servers must install into /app/.venv (use VIRTUAL_ENV env var so pip targets venv)
- The mcp-proxy --port 0 (--sse-port deprecated alias) means random port, must specify
- For env vars to pass to subprocess, use --pass-environment flag
- Command-line args after -- go to the wrapped server
- Some servers need full source not pip package (e.g. arr-suite-mcp has broken pyproject.toml, need git clone + manual cp -r to site-packages)
- mcp-proxy serves both /sse (legacy) and /mcp (streamable HTTP) on the same port simultaneously

- /shared/config/mcp-https/ — nginx:alpine container, host network, port 8443 LAN-only
- Uses SWAG wildcard cert *.mannixbase.duckdns.org via /shared/config/swag/etc/letsencrypt:/etc/letsencrypt:ro mount
- Path-based routing: https://mcp.mannixbase.duckdns.org:8443/<service>/mcp
- nginx config requires: proxy_buffering off, proxy_request_buffering off, proxy_http_version 1.1, long timeouts (86400s), chunked_transfer_encoding on

MCP client configuration formats — important quirks:

CLAUDE CODE (~/.claude.json or via `claude mcp add`):
- Format: {"type": "http", "url": "http://...:port/mcp", "headers": {...optional}}
- Type can be: "http", "sse", "stdio"
- "http" = streamable HTTP (modern, recommended)
- DO NOT put mcpServers in ~/.claude/settings.json — that's deprecated, use ~/.claude.json
- CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> -s user` (user scope = global)

- Only accepts stdio servers in claude_desktop_config.json (command + args format)

- Use the mcp-https gateway with valid wildcard cert

CURSOR/WINDSURF:
- Format: {"serverUrl": "http://..."} (note: serverUrl not url)

PROTOCOL NOTES:
- Streamable HTTP endpoint convention: /mcp (POST + GET)
- Initialize handshake: POST /mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body has method=initialize
- Stateless mode (--stateless on mcp-proxy) means no session_id needed — each request independent
- SSE transport (deprecated) uses /sse endpoint, has session_id, breaks on backend restart
- After mcp-proxy 0.x updates: --sse-port renamed to --port, --sse-host to --host

Two compounding bugs in claude_hooks/claudemem_reindex.py. (1) Windows: subprocess.Popen for any npm-installed .cmd shim (claudemem.cmd, caliber.cmd, etc.) MUST set creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW|DETACHED_PROCESS. The shim's `title %COMSPEC%` line cosmetically labels the cmd window "Administrator:" even though it's not elevated (verified: `whoami /priv` shows only SeChangeNotifyPrivilege). Without these flags the console stays visible for the entire child lifetime — fine for 5s commands, very visible for multi-minute claudemem/bun-mnemex indexing. why we chose stdlib-only http MCP client:
MCP client configuration formats — important quirks:

CLAUDE CODE (~/.claude.json or via `claude mcp add`):
- Format: {"type": "http", "url": "http://...:port/mcp", "headers": {...optional}}
- Type can be: "http", "sse", "stdio"
- "http" = streamable HTTP (modern, recommended)
- DO NOT put mcpServers in ~/.claude/settings.json — that's deprecated, use ~/.claude.json
- CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> -s user` (user scope = global)
- Tool list cached at session start — restart Claude Code with /exit if backend changes

CLAUDE DESKTOP (claude_desktop_config.json):
- Only accepts stdio servers in claude_desktop_config.json (command + args format)
- Remote HTTP/SSE servers MUST be added via GUI: Settings → Connectors → Custom Connector
- Adding remote HTTP entries to the JSON file gets rejected as "not valid mcp servers"
- Claude Desktop also REQUIRES HTTPS for remote connectors (HTTP is rejected)
- Use the mcp-https gateway with valid wildcard cert

CURSOR/WINDSURF:
- Format: {"serverUrl": "http://..."} (note: serverUrl not url)

PROTOCOL NOTES:
- Streamable HTTP endpoint convention: /mcp (POST + GET)
- Initialize handshake: POST /mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body has method=initialize
- Stateless mode (--stateless on mcp-proxy) means no session_id needed — each request independent
- SSE transport (deprecated) uses /sse endpoint, has session_id, breaks on backend restart
- After mcp-proxy 0.x updates: --sse-port renamed to --port, --sse-host to --host

MCP servers architecture on solidPC (2026-04 setup):

ARCHITECTURE:
- All MCP servers run as Docker containers on solidPC (192.168.178.2)
- Each server uses mcp-proxy (ghcr.io/sparfenyuk/mcp-proxy) to wrap a stdio MCP backend and expose Streamable HTTP at /mcp endpoint
- CRITICAL: must use --stateless flag for proper multi-client support (SSE is deprecated in MCP spec)
- All containers use network_mode: host to avoid Docker network pool exhaustion
- Configs at /shared/config/mcp-<name>/

PORT ASSIGNMENTS:
- 32769: searxng (uses sacode/searxng-simple-mcp directly, env TRANSPORT_PROTOCOL=streamable-http)
- 32770: MCPJungle gateway (aggregator, currently unused)
- 32771: arr-suite (Sonarr/Radarr/Lidarr/Prowlarr/Bazarr/Plex)
- 32772: home-assistant (hass-mcp)
- 32773: github
- 32774: filesystem (read-only /shared, /srv)
- 32775: qdrant (semantic memory + Qdrant DB on 6333)
- 32776: memory (knowledge graph)

DOCKERFILE PATTERN for new mcp-proxy-based server:
FROM ghcr.io/sparfenyuk/mcp-proxy:latest
RUN apk add --no-cache nodejs npm && npm install -g <pkg>  # for Node servers
# OR for Python: ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/app/.venv PATH=/app/.venv/bin:$PATH; RUN python -m ensurepip && python -m pip install --no-cache-dir <pkg>
ENTRYPOINT ["mcp-proxy", "--stateless", "--port", "<port>", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--", "<command>"]

KEY GOTCHAS:
- mcp-proxy base image is Alpine with Python 3.13 — use apk not apt, install node via apk
- Python servers must install into /app/.venv (use VIRTUAL_ENV env var so pip targets venv)
- The mcp-proxy --port 0 (--sse-port deprecated alias) means random port, must specify
- For env vars to pass to subprocess, use --pass-environment flag
- Command-line args after -- go to the wrapped server
- Some servers need full source not pip package (e.g. arr-suite-mcp has broken pyproject.toml, need git clone + manual cp -r to site-packages)
- mcp-proxy serves both /sse (legacy) and /mcp (streamable HTTP) on the same port simultaneously

HTTPS GATEWAY (for Claude Desktop which requires HTTPS):
- /shared/config/mcp-https/ — nginx:alpine container, host network, port 8443 LAN-only
- Uses SWAG wildcard cert *.mannixbase.duckdns.org via /shared/config/swag/etc/letsencrypt:/etc/letsencrypt:ro mount
- Path-based routing: https://mcp.mannixbase.duckdns.org:8443/<service>/mcp
- nginx config requires: proxy_buffering off, proxy_request_buffering off, proxy_http_version 1.1, long timeouts (86400s), chunked_transfer_encoding on
- LAN-only via allow 192.168.178.0/24; deny all
- Hostname resolution: needs FritzBox local DNS override OR hosts file on client machine

Claude Desktop with remote HTTP MCP servers — the correct approach (2026-04):

Claude Desktop's claude_desktop_config.json ONLY supports stdio servers (command + args). The "Custom Connector" GUI for remote servers requires cloud OAuth authorization which fails for local/LAN URLs. Direct HTTP/SSE entries in the JSON file are rejected as invalid.

SOLUTION: Use mcp-remote (npm package by geelen) as a stdio→HTTP bridge. Each MCP server entry runs `npx mcp-remote <url>` which spawns a stdio process locally that proxies all calls to the remote HTTP MCP server.

EXAMPLE config for claude_desktop_config.json:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "qdrant": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "http://192.168.178.2:32775/mcp",
        "--allow-http",
        "--transport",
        "http-only"
      ]
    }
  }
}

KEY FLAGS:
- --allow-http: required for non-HTTPS URLs (default rejects http:// for security)
- --transport http-only: skip SSE fallback, force streamable HTTP
- -y on npx: auto-install package without prompting
- mcp-remote also handles OAuth automatically when needed (stores tokens locally)

This means the HTTPS gateway (mcp-https on port 8443) is NOT needed for Claude Desktop. The plain HTTP MCP endpoints (32769-32776) work directly via mcp-remote.

MCP servers architecture on solidPC (2026-04 setup):

ARCHITECTURE:
- All MCP servers run as Docker containers on solidPC (192.168.178.2)
- Each server uses mcp-proxy (ghcr.io/sparfenyuk/mcp-proxy) to wrap a stdio MCP backend and expose Streamable HTTP at /mcp endpoint
- CRITICAL: must use --stateless flag for proper multi-client support (SSE is deprecated in MCP spec)
- All containers use network_mode: host to avoid Docker network pool exhaustion
- Configs at /shared/config/mcp-<name>/

PORT ASSIGNMENTS:
- 32769: searxng (uses sacode/searxng-simple-mcp directly, env TRANSPORT_PROTOCOL=streamable-http)
- 32770: MCPJungle gateway (aggregator, currently unused)
- 32771: arr-suite (Sonarr/Radarr/Lidarr/Prowlarr/Bazarr/Plex)
- 32772: home-assistant (hass-mcp)
- 32773: github
- 32774: filesystem (read-only /shared, /srv)
- 32775: qdrant (semantic memory + Qdrant DB on 6333)
- 32776: memory (knowledge graph)

DOCKERFILE PATTERN for new mcp-proxy-based server:
FROM ghcr.io/sparfenyuk/mcp-proxy:latest
RUN apk add --no-cache nodejs npm && npm install -g <pkg>  # for Node servers
# OR for Python: ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/app/.venv PATH=/app/.venv/bin:$PATH; RUN python -m ensurepip && python -m pip install --no-cache-dir <pkg>
ENTRYPOINT ["mcp-proxy", "--stateless", "--port", "<port>", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--", "<command>"]

KEY GOTCHAS:
- mcp-proxy base image is Alpine with Python 3.13 — use apk not apt, install node via apk
- Python servers must install into /app/.venv (use VIRTUAL_ENV env var so pip targets venv)
- The mcp-proxy --port 0 (--sse-port deprecated alias) means random port, must specify
- For env vars to pass to subprocess, use --pass-environment flag
- Command-line args after -- go to the wrapped server
- Some servers need full source not pip package (e.g. arr-suite-mcp has broken pyproject.toml, need git clone + manual cp -r to site-packages)
- mcp-proxy serves both /sse (legacy) and /mcp (streamable HTTP) on the same port simultaneously

HTTPS GATEWAY (for Claude Desktop which requires HTTPS):
- /shared/config/mcp-https/ — nginx:alpine container, host network, port 8443 LAN-only
- Uses SWAG wildcard cert *.mannixbase.duckdns.org via /shared/config/swag/etc/letsencrypt:/etc/letsencrypt:ro mount
- Path-based routing: https://mcp.mannixbase.duckdns.org:8443/<service>/mcp
- nginx config requires: proxy_buffering off, proxy_request_buffering off, proxy_http_version 1.1, long timeouts (86400s), chunked_transfer_encoding on
- LAN-only via allow 192.168.178.0/24; deny all
- Hostname resolution: needs FritzBox local DNS override OR hosts file on client machine

How to add a new MCP server to solidPC stack — step-by-step:

1. Pick a port from 32777+ (32769-32776 are taken)
2. Create dir: mkdir /shared/config/mcp-<name>/
3. Create Dockerfile (see mcp-servers-architecture entry for template)
4. Create docker-compose.yaml:
   services:
     mcp-<name>:
       build: .
       image: mcp-<name>-proxy:latest
       network_mode: host
       restart: unless-stopped
       labels:
         - com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=false
       # add env_file: .env if secrets needed
       # add volumes if state needs to persist
5. Build and start: cd /shared/config/mcp-<name> && docker compose build && docker compose up -d
6. Test: curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://192.168.178.2:<port>/mcp -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"t","version":"1"}}}' — should return 200
7. Add to Claude Code config: claude mcp add --transport http <name> http://192.168.178.2:<port>/mcp -s user
8. Add HTTPS route in /shared/config/mcp-https/conf/nginx.conf:
   location /<name>/ { proxy_pass http://192.168.178.2:<port>/; }

9. For Claude Desktop: add via GUI Settings→Connectors→Custom Connector with URL https://mcp.mannixbase.duckdns.org:8443/<name>/mcp (DOES NOT work via claude_desktop_config.json — Claude Desktop only accepts stdio servers in that file, remote HTTP must go through GUI)

VERIFICATION COMMANDS:
- Check container running: docker ps --filter "name=mcp-<name>"
- Check logs: docker logs mcp-<name>-mcp-<name>-1 --tail 20
- Check MCP responding: curl above
- Restart all MCP after changes: for d in /shared/config/mcp-*/; do (cd "$d" && docker compose restart); done

MCP client configuration formats — important quirks:

CLAUDE CODE (~/.claude.json or via `claude mcp add`):
- Format: {"type": "http", "url": "http://...:port/mcp", "headers": {...optional}}
- Type can be: "http", "sse", "stdio"
- "http" = streamable HTTP (modern, recommended)
- DO NOT put mcpServers in ~/.claude/settings.json — that's deprecated, use ~/.claude.json
- CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> -s user` (user scope = global)
- Tool list cached at session start — restart Claude Code with /exit if backend changes

CLAUDE DESKTOP (claude_desktop_config.json):
- Only accepts stdio servers in claude_desktop_config.json (command + args format)
- Remote HTTP/SSE servers MUST be added via GUI: Settings → Connectors → Custom Connector
- Adding remote HTTP entries to the JSON file gets rejected as "not valid mcp servers"
- Claude Desktop also REQUIRES HTTPS for remote connectors (HTTP is rejected)
- Use the mcp-https gateway with valid wildcard cert

CURSOR/WINDSURF:
- Format: {"serverUrl": "http://..."} (note: serverUrl not url)

PROTOCOL NOTES:
- Streamable HTTP endpoint convention: /mcp (POST + GET)
- Initialize handshake: POST /mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body has method=initialize
- Stateless mode (--stateless on mcp-proxy) means no session_id needed — each request independent
- SSE transport (deprecated) uses /sse endpoint, has session_id, breaks on backend restart
- After mcp-proxy 0.x updates: --sse-port renamed to --port, --sse-host to --host

Claude Desktop with remote HTTP MCP servers — the correct approach (2026-04):

Claude Desktop's claude_desktop_config.json ONLY supports stdio servers (command + args). The "Custom Connector" GUI for remote servers requires cloud OAuth authorization which fails for local/LAN URLs. Direct HTTP/SSE entries in the JSON file are rejected as invalid.

SOLUTION: Use mcp-remote (npm package by geelen) as a stdio→HTTP bridge. Each MCP server entry runs `npx mcp-remote <url>` which spawns a stdio process locally that proxies all calls to the remote HTTP MCP server.

EXAMPLE config for claude_desktop_config.json:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "qdrant": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "http://192.168.178.2:32775/mcp",
        "--allow-http",
        "--transport",
        "http-only"
      ]
    }
  }
}

KEY FLAGS:
- --allow-http: required for non-HTTPS URLs (default rejects http:// for security)
- --transport http-only: skip SSE fallback, force streamable HTTP
- -y on npx: auto-install package without prompting
- mcp-remote also handles OAuth automatically when needed (stores tokens locally)

This means the HTTPS gateway (mcp-https on port 8443) is NOT needed for Claude Desktop. The plain HTTP MCP endpoints (32769-32776) work directly via mcp-remote.

Requires Node.js installed on the Claude Desktop machine (npx/npm).

CLAUDE CODE (~/.claude.json or via `claude mcp add`):

FROM ghcr.io/sparfenyuk/mcp-proxy:latest
RUN apk add --no-cache nodejs npm && npm install -g <pkg>  # for Node servers
# OR for Python: ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/app/.venv PATH=/app/.venv/bin:$PATH; RUN python -m ensurepip && python -m pip install --no-cache-dir <pkg>
ENTRYPOINT ["mcp-proxy", "--stateless", "--port", "<port>", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--", "<command>"]

- mcp-proxy base image is Alpine with Python 3.13 — use apk not apt, install node via apk
- Python servers must install into /app/.venv (use VIRTUAL_ENV env var so pip targets venv)
- The mcp-proxy --port 0 (--sse-port deprecated alias) means random port, must specify
- For env vars to pass to subprocess, use --pass-environment flag
- Command-line args after -- go to the wrapped server
- Some servers need full source not pip package (e.g. arr-suite-mcp has broken pyproject.toml, need git clone + manual cp -r to site-packages)
- mcp-proxy serves both /sse (legacy) and /mcp (streamable HTTP) on the same port simultaneously

- nginx config requires: proxy_buffering off, proxy_request_buffering off, proxy_http_version 1.1, long timeouts (86400s), chunked_transfer_encoding on

MCP client configuration formats — important quirks:

CLAUDE CODE (~/.claude.json or via `claude mcp add`):
- Format: {"type": "http", "url": "http://...:port/mcp", "headers": {...optional}}
- Type can be: "http", "sse", "stdio"
- "http" = streamable HTTP (modern, recommended)
- DO NOT put mcpServers in ~/.claude/settings.json — that's deprecated, use ~/.claude.json
- CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> -s user` (user scope = global)
- Tool list cached at session start — restart Claude Code with /exit if backend changes

CLAUDE DESKTOP (claude_desktop_config.json):
- Only accepts stdio servers in claude_desktop_config.json (command + args format)
- Remote HTTP/SSE servers MUST be added via GUI: Settings → Connectors → Custom Connector
- Adding remote HTTP entries to the JSON file gets rejected as "not valid mcp servers"
- Claude Desktop also REQUIRES HTTPS for remote connectors (HTTP is rejected)
- Use the mcp-https gateway with valid wildcard cert

CURSOR/WINDSURF:
- Format: {"serverUrl": "http://..."} (note: serverUrl not url)

PROTOCOL NOTES:
- Streamable HTTP endpoint convention: /mcp (POST + GET)
- Initialize handshake: POST /mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body has method=initialize
- Stateless mode (--stateless on mcp-proxy) means no session_id needed — each request independent
- SSE transport (deprecated) uses /sse endpoint, has session_id, breaks on backend restart
- After mcp-proxy 0.x updates: --sse-port renamed to --port, --sse-host to --host

Claude Desktop with remote HTTP MCP servers — the correct approach (2026-04):

Claude Desktop's claude_desktop_config.json ONLY supports stdio servers (command + args). The "Custom Connector" GUI for remote servers requires cloud OAuth authorization which fails for local/LAN URLs. Direct HTTP/SSE entries in the JSON file are rejected as invalid.

SOLUTION: Use mcp-remote (npm package by geelen) as a stdio→HTTP bridge. Each MCP server entry runs `npx mcp-remote <url>` which spawns a stdio process locally that proxies all calls to the remote HTTP MCP server.

EXAMPLE config for claude_desktop_config.json:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "qdrant": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "http://192.168.178.2:32775/mcp",
        "--allow-http",
        "--transport",
        "http-only"
      ]
    }
  }
}

KEY FLAGS:
- --allow-http: required for non-HTTPS URLs (default rejects http:// for security)
- --transport http-only: skip SSE fallback, force streamable HTTP
- -y on npx: auto-install package without prompting
- mcp-remote also handles OAuth automatically when needed (stores tokens locally)

This means the HTTPS gateway (mcp-https on port 8443) is NOT needed for Claude Desktop. The plain HTTP MCP endpoints (32769-32776) work directly via mcp-remote.

Requires Node.js installed on the Claude Desktop machine (npx/npm).

4. Create docker-compose.yaml:

       build: .
       image: mcp-<name>-proxy:latest
       network_mode: host

         - com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=false

7. Add to Claude Code config: claude mcp add --transport http <name> http://192.168.178.2:<port>/mcp -s user
8. Add HTTPS route in /shared/config/mcp-https/conf/nginx.conf:
   location /<name>/ { proxy_pass http://192.168.178.2:<port>/; }

- Check container running: docker ps --filter "name=mcp-<name>"

DERN (Drop Experts Recombine Neurons) - arXiv:2509.10377 - Complete algorithm for MoE expert pruning.

Paper: "Dropping Experts, Recombining Neurons: Retraining-Free Pruning for Sparse MoE LLMs" (EMNLP 2025)
Authors: Yixiao Zhou et al.
Reference implementation: https://github.com/newera-xiao/DERN

THREE-STAGE ALGORITHM:

Stage 1 - Expert Pruning: Score experts by S_i = E[I[i in A(x)] * G_i(x) / sum_j G_j(x)] using calibration data (128 seqs, 2048 tokens from C4). Keep top-k by importance. Implementation also supports weight-norm based scoring: expert_norm * gate_norm.

Stage 2 - Neuron Decomposition and Reassignment:
- Each expert's FFN is decomposed into "neuron segments": seg_i = (w_gate[i,:], w_up[i,:], w_down[:,i]) - one triplet per intermediate neuron
- Segments vectorized as v(seg_i) = concat(w1_i, w2_i, w3_i) in R^{3*hidden_dim}
- For each pruned expert's segment, compute weighted cosine similarity to ALL segments of ALL surviving experts
- Similarity is weighted: w1_weight*cos(w1,w1') + w2_weight*cos(w2,w2') + w3_weight*cos(w3,w3') (default weights 0.0/0.5/0.5 for gate/up/down)
- Assign segment to surviving expert with highest max-similarity if sim >= threshold (default ~0.5)
- Router weight transfer: gate.weight[surviving_idx] += gate.weight[pruned_idx] * (1/n_fragments_in_pruned)

Stage 3 - Intra-Expert Clustering (reconstruction):
- Each surviving expert now has original + transferred segments (possibly > original intermediate_size)
- Run spherical weighted k-means clustering on concatenated segment vectors
- k = target_size = ceil(original_intermediate_size * cluster_ratio), cluster_ratio default 1.0
- Distance metric: cosine with optional per-component feature weights
- Sample weights: importance_score of source expert
- Initialization: top-k segments by max(abs(w1)) + abs(min(w1))
- Norm equalization before centroid computation
- Final centroids are split back into (w1_new, w2_new, w3_new) and become new expert weights

Key details for Gemma 4 adaptation:
- Works with standard gate_proj/up_proj/down_proj MLP structure
- intermediate_size is preserved when cluster_ratio=1.0 (centroids compress back to original size)
- Router gate weights ARE updated (additive transfer proportional to fragment count)
- Supports top-K routing (tested with top-2 Mixtral, top-6 DeepSeek, top-8 Qwen)
- Does NOT require same intermediate_size across experts
- The repo handles Mixtral (w1/w2/w3), DeepSeek, and Qwen model families

MCP client configuration formats — important quirks:

CLAUDE CODE (~/.claude.json or via `claude mcp add`):
- Format: {"type": "http", "url": "http://...:port/mcp", "headers": {...optional}}
- Type can be: "http", "sse", "stdio"
- "http" = streamable HTTP (modern, recommended)
- DO NOT put mcpServers in ~/.claude/settings.json — that's deprecated, use ~/.claude.json
- CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> -s user` (user scope = global)
- Tool list cached at session start — restart Claude Code with /exit if backend changes

CLAUDE DESKTOP (claude_desktop_config.json):
- Only accepts stdio servers in claude_desktop_config.json (command + args format)
- Remote HTTP/SSE servers MUST be added via GUI: Settings → Connectors → Custom Connector
- Adding remote HTTP entries to the JSON file gets rejected as "not valid mcp servers"
- Claude Desktop also REQUIRES HTTPS for remote connectors (HTTP is rejected)
- Use the mcp-https gateway with valid wildcard cert

CURSOR/WINDSURF:
- Format: {"serverUrl": "http://..."} (note: serverUrl not url)

PROTOCOL NOTES:
- Streamable HTTP endpoint convention: /mcp (POST + GET)
- Initialize handshake: POST /mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body has method=initialize
- Stateless mode (--stateless on mcp-proxy) means no session_id needed — each request independent
- SSE transport (deprecated) uses /sse endpoint, has session_id, breaks on backend restart
- After mcp-proxy 0.x updates: --sse-port renamed to --port, --sse-host to --host

MCP client configuration formats — important quirks:

CLAUDE CODE (~/.claude.json or via `claude mcp add`):
- Format: {"type": "http", "url": "http://...:port/mcp", "headers": {...optional}}
- Type can be: "http", "sse", "stdio"
- "http" = streamable HTTP (modern, recommended)
- DO NOT put mcpServers in ~/.claude/settings.json — that's deprecated, use ~/.claude.json
- CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> -s user` (user scope = global)
- Tool list cached at session start — restart Claude Code with /exit if backend changes

CLAUDE DESKTOP (claude_desktop_config.json):
- Only accepts stdio servers in claude_desktop_config.json (command + args format)
- Remote HTTP/SSE servers MUST be added via GUI: Settings → Connectors → Custom Connector
- Adding remote HTTP entries to the JSON file gets rejected as "not valid mcp servers"
- Claude Desktop also REQUIRES HTTPS for remote connectors (HTTP is rejected)
- Use the mcp-https gateway with valid wildcard cert

CURSOR/WINDSURF:
- Format: {"serverUrl": "http://..."} (note: serverUrl not url)

PROTOCOL NOTES:
- Streamable HTTP endpoint convention: /mcp (POST + GET)
- Initialize handshake: POST /mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body has method=initialize
- Stateless mode (--stateless on mcp-proxy) means no session_id needed — each request independent
- SSE transport (deprecated) uses /sse endpoint, has session_id, breaks on backend restart
- After mcp-proxy 0.x updates: --sse-port renamed to --port, --sse-host to --host

why we chose stdlib-only http MCP client:
MCP client configuration formats — important quirks:

CLAUDE CODE (~/.claude.json or via `claude mcp add`):
- Format: {"type": "http", "url": "http://...:port/mcp", "headers": {...optional}}
- Type can be: "http", "sse", "stdio"
- "http" = streamable HTTP (modern, recommended)
- DO NOT put mcpServers in ~/.claude/settings.json — that's deprecated, use ~/.claude.json
- CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> -s user` (user scope = global)
- Tool list cached at session start — restart Claude Code with /exit if backend changes

CLAUDE DESKTOP (claude_desktop_config.json):
- Only accepts stdio servers in claude_desktop_config.json (command + args format)
- Remote HTTP/SSE servers MUST be added via GUI: Settings → Connectors → Custom Connector
- Adding remote HTTP entries to the JSON file gets rejected as "not valid mcp servers"
- Claude Desktop also REQUIRES HTTPS for remote connectors (HTTP is rejected)
- Use the mcp-https gateway with valid wildcard cert

CURSOR/WINDSURF:
- Format: {"serverUrl": "http://..."} (note: serverUrl not url)

PROTOCOL NOTES:
- Streamable HTTP endpoint convention: /mcp (POST + GET)
- Initialize handshake: POST /mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body has method=initialize
- Stateless mode (--stateless on mcp-proxy) means no session_id needed — each request independent
- SSE transport (deprecated) uses /sse endpoint, has session_id, breaks on backend restart
- After mcp-proxy 0.x updates: --sse-port renamed to --port, --sse-host to --host

Claude Desktop with remote HTTP MCP servers — the correct approach (2026-04):

Claude Desktop's claude_desktop_config.json ONLY supports stdio servers (command + args). The "Custom Connector" GUI for remote servers requires cloud OAuth authorization which fails for local/LAN URLs. Direct HTTP/SSE entries in the JSON file are rejected as invalid.

SOLUTION: Use mcp-remote (npm package by geelen) as a stdio→HTTP bridge. Each MCP server entry runs `npx mcp-remote <url>` which spawns a stdio process locally that proxies all calls to the remote HTTP MCP server.

EXAMPLE config for claude_desktop_config.json:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "qdrant": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "http://192.168.178.2:32775/mcp",
        "--allow-http",
        "--transport",
        "http-only"
      ]
    }
  }
}

KEY FLAGS:
- --allow-http: required for non-HTTPS URLs (default rejects http:// for security)
- --transport http-only: skip SSE fallback, force streamable HTTP
- -y on npx: auto-install package without prompting
- mcp-remote also handles OAuth automatically when needed (stores tokens locally)

This means the HTTPS gateway (mcp-https on port 8443) is NOT needed for Claude Desktop. The plain HTTP MCP endpoints (32769-32776) work directly via mcp-remote.

Requires Node.js installed on the Claude Desktop machine (npx/npm).

Two compounding bugs in claude_hooks/claudemem_reindex.py. (1) Windows: subprocess.Popen for any npm-installed .cmd shim (claudemem.cmd, caliber.cmd, etc.) MUST set creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW|DETACHED_PROCESS. The shim's `title %COMSPEC%` line cosmetically labels the cmd window "Administrator:" even though it's not elevated (verified: `whoami /priv` shows only SeChangeNotifyPrivilege). Without these flags the console stays visible for the entire child lifetime — fine for 5s commands, very visible for multi-minute claudemem/bun-mnemex indexing. POSIX: start_new_session=True is enough. (2) Pile-up: a timestamp-only lock with 60s cooldown is useless once the indexer takes 5+ minutes. Every Stop hook past the cooldown spawned another concurrent reindex. Fix: lock format is now `<pid>\n<unix-ts>`, _acquire_lock first checks _pid_running(pid) (Windows: ctypes OpenProcess+GetExitCodeProcess, STILL_ACTIVE=259; POSIX: kill(pid,0)) and refuses regardless of age if the lock-named PID is alive. - Format: {"type": "http", "url": "http://...:port/mcp", "headers": {...optional}}
- Type can be: "http", "sse", "stdio"
- "http" = streamable HTTP (modern, recommended)
- DO NOT put mcpServers in ~/.claude/settings.json — that's deprecated, use ~/.claude.json
- CLI: `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> -s user` (user scope = global)
- Tool list cached at session start — restart Claude Code with /exit if backend changes

CLAUDE DESKTOP (claude_desktop_config.json):
- Only accepts stdio servers in claude_desktop_config.json (command + args format)
- Remote HTTP/SSE servers MUST be added via GUI: Settings → Connectors → Custom Connector
- Adding remote HTTP entries to the JSON file gets rejected as "not valid mcp servers"
- Claude Desktop also REQUIRES HTTPS for remote connectors (HTTP is rejected)
- Use the mcp-https gateway with valid wildcard cert

CURSOR/WINDSURF:
- Format: {"serverUrl": "http://..."} (note: serverUrl not url)

PROTOCOL NOTES:
- Streamable HTTP endpoint convention: /mcp (POST + GET)
- Initialize handshake: POST /mcp with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, body has method=initialize
- Stateless mode (--stateless on mcp-proxy) means no session_id needed — each request independent
- SSE transport (deprecated) uses /sse endpoint, has session_id, breaks on backend restart
- After mcp-proxy 0.x updates: --sse-port renamed to --port, --sse-host to --host

Claude Desktop with remote HTTP MCP servers — the correct approach (2026-04):

Claude Desktop's claude_desktop_config.json ONLY supports stdio servers (command + args). The "Custom Connector" GUI for remote servers requires cloud OAuth authorization which fails for local/LAN URLs. Direct HTTP/SSE entries in the JSON file are rejected as invalid.

SOLUTION: Use mcp-remote (npm package by geelen) as a stdio→HTTP bridge. Each MCP server entry runs `npx mcp-remote <url>` which spawns a stdio process locally that proxies all calls to the remote HTTP MCP server.

EXAMPLE config for claude_desktop_config.json:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "qdrant": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "http://192.168.178.2:32775/mcp",
        "--allow-http",
        "--transport",
        "http-only"
      ]
    }
  }
}

KEY FLAGS:
- --allow-http: required for non-HTTPS URLs (default rejects http:// for security)
- --transport http-only: skip SSE fallback, force streamable HTTP
- -y on npx: auto-install package without prompting
- mcp-remote also handles OAuth automatically when needed (stores tokens locally)

This means the HTTPS gateway (mcp-https on port 8443) is NOT needed for Claude Desktop. The plain HTTP MCP endpoints (32769-32776) work directly via mcp-remote.
